title: Volume incentive model for embeddings & rerank: slotless credits + time-bound burst offers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running high-throughput semantic search and reranking workloads are sensitive to per-vector unit pricing and see uneven value from bulk slab discounts. We need a pricing experiment that: 1) preserves predictable unit economics for small customers, 2) gives meaningful incentives for high-volume customers without adding a complex slab matrix, and 3) remains auditable for QSA/enterprise contract flows. This ticket defines an experiment for a slotless credit model (time-bound credits that spend down based on vector units) combined with a transient burst offer to evaluate elasticity and churn impact.
experiment_design: Variant A (Control): current per-vector pricing with existing slab tiers. Variant B (Slotless Credits): customers purchase credits (1 credit = 1 standard vector-unit) that expire monthly; discounts are applied at purchase time (volume bands), not at invoice time. Variant C (Burst Offer): same as B but with a 14-day promotional multiplier (e.g., 1.5x credits on top of purchase for the first cycle) to simulate burst discount behavior. Enrollment: randomize new and qualifying existing customers (usage > 250k vector-units/month) into cohorts for 12 weeks. Billing mechanics: credits consumed first; overage billed at published per-vector rate. Edge cases: partial consumption, refunds, contract credits. We'll instrument usage with per-customer credit burn logs and tie to payouts in billing system.
success_metrics: Primary: net revenue per active customer (NRAC) over 12 weeks, churn delta vs control, and average cost-per-1000-vector-units to company (post-discount). Secondary: average conversion rate from trial to paid for high-volume customers, change in peak utilization, customer-reported value (NPS/survey). Safety gates: if week-over-week revenue drops > 10% for cohort or churn increases > 3 percentage points, pause promotional cohort.
rollout_plan: 1) Legal & QSA checklist completed (see artifacts). 2) Internal pilot with 3 enterprise customers (opt-in) for two billing cycles to validate mechanics. 3) Feature flag release for credit purchase UI + API support. 4) Randomized experiment across eligible customers after pilot. 5) Post-analysis and recommendation for pricing ladder replacement or hybrid implementation. Timeline: pilot (2 weeks), infra build and API (3 weeks), experiment (12 weeks), analysis (2 weeks).
qsa_preparation: Prepare a QSA appendix describing: credit expiration policy, audit logs for credit issuance and burn, KMS handling of billing artifacts, and clear mapping between credits and vector-unit definitions. Include sample contract language for credits, refund/termination clauses, and certificate of pricing computation. Coordinate with Legal to pre-clear addendum for enterprise contracts. Request security_review_required: true.
notes: Design and billing engineering need to sync on fractional vector units for hybrid models. Finance requested a conservative 90-day runway projection for revenue risk. PM to coordinate customer outreach for pilot opt-ins; target three customers across verticals (search, commerce, knowledge base).
